usage: the shirt is a bit big
examples: Today I wear a white shirt.
I want to buy a shirt.
nuance: 셔츠 is worn on the upper body, so Koreans always use the verb 입다, never 신다 or 쓰다. To count clothing they use the counter 벌, not 개.
mistakes: Using 신다 instead of 입다 for a shirt

examples: I want to buy comfortable pants.
nuance: 바지 is always singular in Korean even though English uses pants as plural, so you never add a plural ending. Like all body clothing it takes the verb 입다.
mistakes: Adding a plural ending like the English word

examples: This skirt is a bit short.
I want to buy a pretty skirt.
nuance: 치마 is worn on the lower body and uses the verb 입다 just like other clothes. Korean does not change the verb for skirts, unlike shoes which use 신다.
mistakes: Using 신다 instead of 입다 for a skirt

examples: In winter I wear a thick coat.
I want to buy a new coat.
nuance: 코트 is a loanword for a warm outer layer worn in winter, and like all clothing it uses the verb 입다. Koreans pronounce every syllable of the borrowed word evenly.
mistakes: Using 쓰다 instead of 입다 for a coat

examples: It is hot so I wear a hat.
I want to buy a warm hat.
nuance: 모자 goes on your head, so Koreans use the verb 쓰다, not 입다 which is only for body clothing. The same verb 쓰다 is also used for glasses.
mistakes: Using 입다 instead of 쓰다 for a hat

examples: It is cold so I wear thick socks.
Give me one pair of socks, please.
nuance: 양말 goes on the feet, so Koreans use the verb 신다 like shoes, never 입다. A pair is counted with the special counter 켤레, not 개.
mistakes: Using 입다 instead of 신다 for socks

examples: I want to buy new gloves.
nuance: 장갑 fits onto the hands, so Koreans most naturally use the verb 끼다 rather than 입다. Like socks a pair is counted with the counter 켤레.
mistakes: Using 입다 instead of 끼다 for gloves

examples: It is cold so I wear a scarf.
I want to buy a warm scarf.
nuance: 목도리 wraps around the neck, and the most natural verb is 하다 or 두르다, not 입다. Beginners can safely say 목도리를 하다 in daily life.
mistakes: Using 입다 instead of 하다 for a scarf

examples: My eyesight is bad so I wear glasses.
I want to buy new glasses.
nuance: 안경 sits on your face, so Koreans use the verb 쓰다, the same verb used for hats. To put them on you say 안경을 쓰다, never 입다 or 신다.
mistakes: Using 입다 instead of 쓰다 for glasses

examples: I wear a watch every day.
I want to buy a good watch.
nuance: 시계 on the wrist uses the special verb 차다, meaning to fasten on, not 입다. The same word 시계 also means a wall clock, so context decides.
mistakes: Using 입다 instead of 차다 for a wristwatch

examples: I wear sneakers when I exercise.
I want to buy new sneakers.
nuance: 운동화 are athletic shoes for the feet, so Koreans use the verb 신다, never 입다. Like all footwear a pair is counted with the counter 켤레.
mistakes: Using 입다 instead of 신다 for sneakers

examples: I wear dress shoes to work.
These dress shoes are a bit uncomfortable.
I want to buy comfortable dress shoes.
nuance: 구두 are formal leather shoes for the feet, so they take the verb 신다 like all footwear. Do not confuse 구두 the shoes with the casual sneakers 운동화.
mistakes: Using 입다 instead of 신다 for dress shoes
